author: Autodesk
description: An example graph demonstrating how to use the simulate_rods solver to apply secondary animation on a wobbling plant's skeleton.

metadata.author: Autodesk
metadata.description: An example graph demonstrating how to use the simulate_rods solver to apply secondary animation on a wobbling plant's skeleton.

_notes.text: Create the plant skeleton. The `joint_parent_index` and `joint_pivot_matrix` values are hard-coded in two `value` nodes to provide the initial skeleton structure of the plant in a standalone graph. After constructing the skeleton from the raw data, we update the joint transforms so that all transform related geo properties are properly precomputed.

Compute additional geo properties that will be used by the `simulate_rods` downstream. First, we compute a `joint_is_trunk` geo properties to identify which joints are part of the trunk of the plant. Then, we compute the `joint_size` to make some joints thicker, and other joints thinner. Finally, we cache the skeleton to avoid recomputing it since it is not supposed to change every time the graph evaluates.

Use the `joint_is_trunk` geo property data to create different simulation property values for the trunk and the branches, in order to make the trunk stiffer and the branches looser. We also use the `joint_size` geo property to define the `thickness` of the rod points to make larger joints heavier.

_backdrops.title: Update joint transforms from simulation result
Create a matrix using the vector as rotation or translation depending on the animation mode.
Transform all joint pivots by the matrix we just created. This will make the whole skeleton move from the origin.

_notes.text: Compute the joint sizes using the joint lengths. We use `change_range` to modulate the length values and create larger sizes near the root and smaller sizes when we are further down the hierarchy. Finally, we use the `joint_is_trunk` geo property to scale the sizes further before applying them on the skeleton.

_backdrops.title: Tag all trunk joints using the first chain's joint indices.
